definitions: To make a place tidy and free of dirt or mess.
To improve the appearance or condition of something.
To make a large profit or gain a significant advantage, often in a competitive situation.
To stop engaging in illegal or immoral activities.
examples: They cleaned up the park after the festival.
The new software cleaned up the data entry process.
Our team cleaned up at the championship.
He cleaned up his act after getting into trouble.
pastTenses: cleaned up (past simple), cleaned up (present perfect), cleaned up (past perfect)
